title: Thornwick Border Guard
summary: Four-piece Warrior set found in Acts I and II, built for frontline border guards holding muddy river crossings.
infobox: Act I–II Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Warrior Set)

list: 3 pieces: +45 Max HP and +15% Poison/Cold Resistance
4 pieces: Hold the Line grants nearby mercenaries +6 Armor

p: Standard kit issued to the twelve-year border veterans who held the Redwater fords long after the capital stopped sending pay-wagons.

Issued to the Thornwick picket companies before the Salt Tithe stripped the armories bare. Each plate bears a stamped alder leaf and the rust of three wet winters. Veterans swear the gorget sits crooked until it takes its first gnoll axe.

title: Caldera Siege-Breaker
summary: Endgame four-piece Warrior set from Act IV and Hard+ content, forged for breaking heavy caldera fortifications.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Warrior Set)

list: 2 pieces: +18 Melee Damage and +8 Armor Penetration
3 pieces: +30% Fire Resistance and +80 Max HP
4 pieces: Melee criticals sunder 6 Armor and trigger a shockwave

p: Hammered over open volcanic cracks in Ironcamp by Forgemaster Vok for the vanguard tasked with cracking the Gauntlet of Iron.

Hammered in the smoky foundry sheds of Ironcamp for sappers who expected to die against basalt walls. The joints are packed with tallow and soot so volcanic grit cannot lock the elbows. Few full suits survive a single breach intact.

title: Greywood Fen-Stalker
summary: Four-piece Archer set dropping in Acts II and III, tailored for quiet stalking through dense timber and bog.
infobox: Act II–III Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Archer Set)

list: 3 pieces: +12% Critical Chance and +2 Vision Radius
4 pieces: First shot from cover deals +50% Crit Damage and roots 2s

p: Worn by border poachers and Redmarsh toll-marksmen who learned that unseen boots live three winters longer than loud armor.

Stitched from oil-rubbed deerhide and dyed with alder bark by hunters who refused to pay the Crown's game tax. Gamekeepers once hanged men for wearing these cuffs in Thornwick. Now the same bailiffs hire them to scout the fen.

title: Harborwall Windlass Corps
summary: Act IV and Hard+ four-piece Archer set designed for heavy windlass marksmen defending coastal walls.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Archer Set)

list: 3 pieces: +20% Ranged Attack Speed and +20% Cold Resistance
4 pieces: Every third bolt pierces in a line for 140% weapon damage

p: Tailored for Gate Warden Lyra's coastal pickets who held Oakhaven's sea-walls against armored privateers with windlass bolts and roof-slates.

Oakhaven's harbor masters outfitted their parapet crews in salt-cured leather reinforced with brass hooks for spanning heavy prods. The left sleeve is always worn smooth from resting against wet granite. Every piece smells faintly of tar.

title: Collegium Thermodynamicist
summary: Four-piece Mage set from Acts III and IV, worn by arcanists who measure heat, flux, and ley-line strain.
infobox: Act III–IV Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Mage Set)

list: 2 pieces: +45 Max Mana and +1.8 Mana Regen/s
3 pieces: +20% Fire and Lightning Spell Damage
4 pieces: Casting a fire spell empowers your next lightning spell by +35%

p: Assembled by expelled mint-assayers who proved that imperial state liturgy was merely poorly documented thermal engineering.

Tailored for Collegium fellows dispatched to audit failing border wards and smelters. Copper thread runs through the hems to bleed off stray sparks before they catch the wool. Most owners pawned the silver clasps during the retreat.

title: Celestial Spire Magister
summary: High-tier four-piece Mage set from Act IV and Hard+ Endgame, reserved for senior celestial arcanists.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Mage Set)

list: 2 pieces: +10 Intelligence and +20% All Elemental Resistances
3 pieces: -20% Spell Mana Costs and +15% Cast Speed
4 pieces: 20% chance for any spell cast to trigger a free Astral Nova

p: Relic vestments preserved in Oakhaven's sealed vaults, woven to channel raw ley-currents without scorching the bearer's knuckles.

Once worn only in the drafty upper galleries of the Spire Conclave during winter deliberations. The indigo cloth resists soot and ash far better than ordinary linen. Finding a complete suit in the field usually means a magister never came back.

title: Lower-Parish Probate Clerk
summary: Early four-piece Necromancer set from Acts I and II, worn by clerks who audit both the living and the dead.
infobox: Act I–II Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Necromancer Set)

list: 2 pieces: +25% Raised Servant HP and +1 Max Servant
3 pieces: +18% Curse & DoT Damage and +1.5 Mana Regen/s
4 pieces: Slain cursed foes rise automatically as indentured skeletons

p: Kept by Thornwick's mortuary clerks who discovered that delinquent tax liens remain legally enforceable long after the debtor's funeral.

Lower-parish probate officers wore these drab vestments while tallying unpaid debts at pauper graves. Ink stains the cuffs permanently, and the pockets are sized for wax seals and brass scales. Even the dead hesitate to argue with a stamped writ.

title: Coastal Abbey Oath-Keeper
summary: Four-piece Necromancer set found in Acts III and IV, belonging to coastal oath-keepers who bind restless spirits.
infobox: Act III–IV Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Necromancer Set)

list: Ivory Testament Ritual Rod (Crystal Siphon Wand)
2 pieces: +25% Healing & Shield Power and +20% Mind Resistance
4 pieces: Forgive the Oath restores 30% Mana and grants 3s Invulnerability

p: Vestments of the coastal scriptorium arbiters who bound unquiet sailors' ghosts to honor deathbed promises before releasing them to rest.

Woven in the damp scriptoriums of the coastal abbeys where monks kept watch over drowned sailors. Lead weights sewn into the hem keep the robes from whipping in sea gales. Each piece carries a quiet salt-blessing against grave-rot.

title: Redmarsh Salt-Caravan Guard
summary: Acts III and IV four-piece Warrior set built for guards escorting salt wagons across hostile alkali flats.
infobox: Act III–IV Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Warrior Set)

list: 2 pieces: +20% Poison & Fire Resistance and +10% Movement Speed
3 pieces: +35 Max HP and +15% Gold Found
4 pieces: Potions heal +40% more and cleanse poison and bleed

p: Practical gear pieced together by Quartermaster Bram's outriders who survived the alkali flats by valuing clean water above heraldry.

Redmarsh drovers learned early that bright steel blinds the wearer and cooks the flesh underneath. These plates are dulled with vinegar and backed with woven horsehair to keep out alkali dust. Surviving guards rarely sell their kit.

title: First Watch Threshold Remnant
summary: Endgame four-piece Necromancer set from Act IV and Hard+, salvaged from the ancient sentinels of the Threshold.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Necromancer Set)

list: Anchor-Seal Cosmos Eye (Eye of the Cosmos)
First-Watch Brass Medallion (Medallion of the Celestial Spire)
2 pieces: +12 Intelligence and +25% Raised Servant Damage
3 pieces: +25% All Resistances and +60 Max Mana
4 pieces: Summons an elite First Watch Bailiff whenever a boss phase shifts

p: Salvaged from the obsidian steps below the Threshold Chamber, still warm with the unfulfilled oaths of Thornvael's original wardens.

Recovered from cracked stone alcoves where the First Watch kept vigil long before the Southern Crown existed. The cloth feels dry as old parchment yet refuses to tear under a blade. Quartermasters refuse to log these pieces after sundown.

title: Alder Ford Toll-Bow
summary: Four-piece Archer set from Acts I and II, issued to bowmen stationed at the river toll-towers.
infobox: Act I–II Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Archer Set)

list: 2 pieces: +10 Accuracy and +6% Critical Strike Chance
3 pieces: +30 Max HP and +15% Cold Resistance
4 pieces: Ranged attacks against targets in water or mud deal +15% Damage

p: Worn by the river-wardens who guarded the crossing tariffs between Thornwick and the northern border tracks before the garrisons mutinied.

Alder Ford toll-collectors learned that a polite clerk with a ledger gets robbed, while a clerk with a bow gets paid. These hooded jerkins shed freezing river drizzle for hours on watch. The quivers are waxed shut against morning fog.

title: Wayshrine Hedgemage
summary: Acts I and II four-piece Mage set stitched together by wandering arcanists who tend roadside wayshrines.
infobox: Act I–II Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Mage Set)

list: 2 pieces: +14 Spell Damage and +25 Max Mana
3 pieces: +8% Cast Speed and +12% Fire Resistance
4 pieces: Casting a bolt spell restores 6 Mana when standing still

p: Assembled by wandering border tutors who traded weather-charms and literacy lessons for dry barn lofts along the Redwater.

Not every caster earned a Collegium stipend; most learned their craft copying smudged almanacs by tallow light. This kit pairs patched wool with copper-wire charms traded for mending roofs and curing cattle. It looks humble, which keeps bandits careless.

title: Sunken Dike Sentinel
summary: Four-piece Warrior set dropping in Acts II and III, made for sentinels patrolling flooded canals and seawalls.
infobox: Act II–III Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Warrior Set)

list: 3 pieces: +65 Max HP and +10% Armor Penetration
4 pieces: Taking poison damage grants +8 Armor for 6 seconds

p: Forged for the penal battalions ordered to hold Redmarsh's crumbling earthen dikes against bog-beasts and heretic raiders alike.

Dike wardens spend half their shift knee-deep in brackish water, so their armor is lacquered with pitch and fish oil. The joints creak like wet rope, and the boots drain through punched heel-holes. Nothing short of a tide-surge moves them.

title: Quicklime Parish Sexton
summary: Acts II and III four-piece Necromancer set worn by parish gravediggers who seal corpses in quicklime.
infobox: Act II–III Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Necromancer Set)

list: 2 pieces: +20% Minion Max HP and +16 Spell Damage
3 pieces: +22% Poison Resistance and +10% Cast Speed
4 pieces: Your raised minions leave a toxic cloud on death

p: Garments of the grim Redmarsh grave-keepers who learned that burying corpses in wet peat only invited them to walk again.

In the warm alkali bogs, bodies do not stay buried unless weighted and limed properly. Sextons wear heavy waxed aprons and bone-handled tools that double as ward-anchors. Travelers give them wide berth, mostly for the smell.

title: Bitter-Root Fen-Doctor
summary: Four-piece Mage set from Acts II and III, crafted for marsh healers who brew bitter roots and antitoxins.
infobox: Act II–III Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Mage Set)

list: 2 pieces: +18 Spell Damage and +10 Mana Regeneration
3 pieces: +55 Max HP and +25% Poison Resistance
4 pieces: Healing potions also grant +15% Spell Damage for 8 seconds

p: Worn by quarantine physicians who braved the fever-wards of Redmarsh long after royal magistrates abandoned the province.

Fen-doctors carry more glass phials than coin, stitched into oiled pockets that survive a fall in the peat. Their masks are stuffed with dried rue and wormwood to dull the marsh stink. Half their remedies cure fever; the rest settle scores.

title: Breakwater Boarding Corps
summary: Four-piece Warrior set from Acts III and IV, worn by shock troops who board hostile vessels along the Iron Coast.
infobox: Act III–IV Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Warrior Set)

list: 3 pieces: +85 Max HP and +25% Cold/Lightning Resistance
4 pieces: Blocking a melee hit deals 18 physical damage back to the attacker

p: Standard heavy kit of the Ironcamp cliff-marines who repelled corsair landing craft along the jagged basalt coves.

Built for narrow decks and slippery gangplanks where a fall in full plate means drowning. The pauldrons are notched to catch boarding hooks, and every buckle releases with one yank. Harborwatch veterans still swear by its balance.

title: Shingle-Reef Smuggler
summary: Endgame four-piece Archer set from Act IV and Hard+, favored by smugglers who work the rocky shingle reefs.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Archer Set)

list: 2 pieces: +24 Ranged Damage and +12% Dodge Chance
3 pieces: +14% Critical Strike Chance and +20 Accuracy
4 pieces: Dodging an attack grants +15% Attack Speed for 4 seconds

p: Favored by Iron Coast wreck-scavengers and smugglers who navigated razor-sharp sea-cliffs under cover of winter squalls.

Cliff-runners know every blind cove between Oakhaven and the reefs, moving cargo on moonless nights with muffled boots. Their gear is dark wool and oiled rawhide, with brass clips dulled in chimney soot. Customs men rarely catch them alive.

title: Cliff-Ossuary Tide-Caller
summary: Acts III and IV four-piece Necromancer set belonging to sea-ossuary callers who command drowned spirits.
infobox: Act III–IV Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Necromancer Set)

list: 2 pieces: +28% Minion Damage and +25 Spell Damage
3 pieces: +65 Max Mana and +25% Cold Resistance
4 pieces: Summoning a minion chills nearby enemies for 3 seconds

p: Relics of the solitary cliff-hermits who bound drowned mariners to guard the coastal ossuaries against pirate grave-robbers.

Where the cliffs drop straight into black water, coastal necromancers lower iron bells to summon what the currents kept. These salt-stiffened vestments are lined with bleached kelp and silver wire. The hems stay damp even in the desert.

title: Pyre-Marshal's Executioners
summary: Act IV and Hard+ four-piece Warrior set worn by heavy executioners serving the Pyre-Marshal.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Warrior Set)

list: Slag-Scarred Citadel Aegis (Aegis of the Citadel)
3 pieces: +120 Max HP and +22 Armor Penetration
4 pieces: Melee attacks ignite enemies for 24 fire damage over 3 seconds

p: Forged in the royal gunpowder foundries for the Sovereign's inner-wall shock troops during the final siege of Crown and Ember.

Forged from slag-quenched steel that turns dull crimson when heated near volcanic vents. The vanguard troops who wore it marched into sulfur trenches without flinching. Most suits found today were pried off men who refused to yield an inch.

title: Sovereign Hearth-Archon
summary: Endgame four-piece Mage set from Act IV and Hard+, tailored for archons who channel volcanic heat.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Champions, Boss Chests, Tavern Bounties & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Mage Set)

list: Molten-Bronze Bell Sphere (Eye of the Cosmos)
2 pieces: +42 Spell Damage and +80 Max Mana
3 pieces: +16% Spell Critical Chance and +35% Fire Resistance
4 pieces: Fire spells reduce target Fire Resistance by 15% for 5 seconds

p: Vestments of the capital's high court pyromancers, who reduced entire rebellious districts to vitrified glass on royal decree.

Woven from asbestos thread and charred silk so the wearer's sleeves do not catch fire during long incantations. Senior hearth-archons wore these robes while calibrating the caldera furnaces. Ordinary tailors refuse to touch the scorching fabric.

title: Iron Warden's Bastion
summary: Four-piece Warrior set from Acts II and III elite packs, built as a heavy defensive bastion on the march.
infobox: Act II–III Elite Packs, Super-Uniques & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Warrior Set)

list: Iron Warden's Visor (Helm, T3) — The slit visor of Commander Valerius, who held the river breach against forty waves of invaders.
Iron Warden's Tower (Shield, T3) — Inlaid with the crest of the vigilant wolf, ringing like a cathedral bell under heavy blows.
Iron Warden's Hauberk (Armor, T3) — Scored by claws and arrows, this chestpiece refused to bend even when the bastion fell.
Iron Warden's Greaves (Boots, T3) — Weighted with cold-rolled steel, rooting the defender firmly into bloody soil.

p: Commissioned by provincial marshals who needed officers to survive ambush volleys on open roads. The overlapping plates rattle like a wagon full of kettles, yet turn aside bodkin shafts with ease. Only broad-shouldered veterans last a day in it.

title: Pyromancer's Ember-Veil
summary: Three-piece Mage set dropping from Acts II and III elites, focused on channeling raw flame without burning the caster.
infobox: Act II–III Elite Packs, Super-Uniques & Mystery Gamble (3-Piece Mage Set)

list: Robe of the Blazing Core (Armor, T3)

p: A compact traveling kit favored by field pyromancers who cannot haul a full trunk of vestments across the wastes. Soot darkens the collar after the first week of campaigning. Its brass clasps stay warm to the touch even in rain.

title: Shadow-Stalker's Silent Walk
summary: Universal three-piece set for any class from Acts II and III elites, prized for quiet movement and swift strikes.
infobox: Act II–III Elite Packs, Super-Uniques & Mystery Gamble (3-Piece All Set)

p: Smugglers, scouts, and disgraced clerks all covet these slate-gray garments for the same reason: nobody hears you coming. The soles are stitched with layered felt that mutes footsteps on wet flagstones. Bailiffs confiscate it on sight.

title: Alder Vanguard's Regalia
summary: Four-piece all-class set from Acts I and II elites, representing the standard officer regalia of the Alder front.
infobox: Act I–II Elite Packs, Super-Uniques & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece All Set)

p: Before the river line broke, the Alder Vanguard marched in matched wool and polished iron paid for by northern tolls. Now the pieces turn up scattered in bandit camps and pawnshops. Wearing a full set still earns a quiet nod from old soldiers.

title: Redmarsh Reaver's Armament
summary: Four-piece Warrior set from Acts III and IV elites, stripped from ruthless desert raiders and mercenary captains.
infobox: Act III–IV Elite Packs, Super-Uniques & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Warrior Set)

p: Reaver captains hammer captured imperial armor into lighter, sharper shapes suited for fast canyon raids. The edges are filed deliberately rough to catch enemy blades and tear cloak hems. Quartermasters pay extra just to get it off the roads.

title: Boreal Frost-Weaver's Shroud
summary: Acts III and IV four-piece Mage set from elite packs, woven to hold bitter winter cold against volcanic heat.
infobox: Act III–IV Elite Packs, Super-Uniques & Mystery Gamble (4-Piece Mage Set)

list: 3 pieces: +50 Mana, +2 Def, +2 Abs, +18% Spell Power, Resists 0/25/20/0/0

p: Brought south by northern arcanists who never trusted the dry winds of Redmarsh. Tiny beads of hoarfrost form along the cuffs whenever the wearer draws mana. In the caldera approaches, merchants would trade a horse for the cloak alone.

title: Crown-Forged Juggernaut
summary: Five-piece endgame Warrior set from Act IV and Hard+ elites, crafted in the royal foundries for unstoppable shock troops.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Elite Packs, Super-Uniques & Mystery Gamble (5-Piece Warrior Set)

p: Stamped with the Southern Crown's assay mark, these massive plates were meant to break rebel barricades in a single charge. Few smiths outside the capital knew how to temper the pauldrons without cracking them. Wearing all five pieces feels like carrying a gate.

title: Astral Sovereign's Regalia
summary: Five-piece endgame Mage set from Act IV and Hard+ elites, channeling high-order astral power for master casters.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Elite Packs, Super-Uniques & Mystery Gamble (5-Piece Mage Set)

list: 4 pieces: +40 HP, +80 Mana, +3 Def, +2 Abs, +15% Spell Power
5 pieces: +60 HP, +120 Mana, +3 Abs, +35% Spell Power, Resists 25/25/25/25/25

p: Designed for senior conclave envoys who mediated disputes between noble houses and the Synod. Star-silver thread traces ley-geometry across the shoulders and hem. Those who assemble all five pieces rarely answer to mortal magistrates anymore.
